title: 唐詩八首
author: 李白、王維等
blurb: Eight short, famous Tang poems, mostly four lines each, ideal for your first real reading.
note: Tang dynasty poems from the 8th century, in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Guo Xi, Early Spring (早春图), 1072. National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 孔乙己
author: 鲁迅
blurb: A short story about a failed scholar who drinks at a village tavern, one of the most famous works of modern Chinese fiction.
note: Published in 1919, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Lu Xun in Shanghai, 1 May 1933. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 故乡
author: 鲁迅
blurb: A man returns to his hometown and finds that both the place and his childhood friend have changed.
note: Published in 1921, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Ma Yuan, Angler on a Wintry Lake (寒江独钓图), about 1195. Tokyo National Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 狂人日记
author: 鲁迅
blurb: China's first modern vernacular short story, the diary of a man who fears everyone around him wants to eat him.
note: Published in 1918, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Lu Xun at fifty, Shanghai, September 1930. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 論語·學而
author: 孔子弟子
blurb: The first chapter of the Analects, sixteen short sayings on learning and character, in classical Chinese.
note: Composed more than 2,000 years ago, in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Confucius at leisure (孔子燕居像), anonymous. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 西遊記 第一回
author: 吳承恩
blurb: The Monkey King is born from a stone, finds a home at Flower-Fruit Mountain, and sets out to learn immortality.
note: Written in the 16th century, in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Sun Wukong on a cloud, woodblock illustration to Journey to the West. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 西遊記
author: 吳承恩
blurb: The Monkey King, Tang Sanzang and their companions travel west for the scriptures. Complete, all 100 chapters of the Ming novel Journey to the West.
note: Wu Cheng'en, 16th century; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource, Shidetang-based edition.
coverCredit: Cover of the Ming edition of Li Zhuowu’s commented Journey to the West, illustrations volume. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 紅樓夢
author: 曹雪芹、高鶚
blurb: The rise and fall of the Jia family and the tragic love of Baoyu and Daiyu. Complete, all 120 chapters of Dream of the Red Chamber.
note: Cao Xueqin (ch. 1-80) and Gao E (ch. 81-120), 18th century; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource collated edition (Gengchen base for 1-80, Cheng-jia for 81-120).
coverCredit: Sun Wen, the Garden of Grand View (大观园), 19th century. Lüshun Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 三國演義
author: 羅貫中
blurb: Heroes and schemers fight over the fallen Han empire: Liu Bei, Cao Cao, Zhuge Liang. Complete, all 120 chapters of Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
note: Luo Guanzhong, 14th century, in the Mao Zonggang revision; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource.
coverCredit: Shang Xi, Guan Yu Captures General Pang De (关羽擒将图), 15th century. Palace Museum, Beijing. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 水滸傳
author: 施耐庵
blurb: 108 outlaws gather at Liangshan Marsh. Complete, all 120 chapters of Water Margin.
note: Shi Nai'an, 14th century; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource, the 120-chapter Yuan Wuya edition.
coverCredit: Chen Hongshou, Yang Zhi, from the Water Margin cards (水浒叶子), 17th century. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
